chunks: Ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Hisham ibn Salim, Murazim, and Shu'ayb, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام:
Regarding a man performing tamattu‘ who enters on the night of Arafah, then performs tawaf and sa‘i, then enters ihram and comes to Mina, he عليه السلام said: “There is no harm.”

key_terms.فَيَطُوفُ: he performs tawaf around the Ka'bah
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; it is unobjectionable
key_terms.لَيْلَةَ عَرَفَةَ: the night before the standing of Arafah
key_terms.مِنًى: Mina, the sacred site to which pilgrims proceed during Hajj
key_terms.وَيَسْعَى: he performs sa‘i between al-Safa and al-Marwah
key_terms.يُحْرِمُ: he enters the state of ihram

ai.seo_question: Is there any harm if a pilgrim performing tamattu‘ enters on the night of Arafah, performs tawaf and sa‘i, then enters ihram and goes to Mina?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the timing and sequence of rites in Hajj al-tamattu‘. It indicates that if a person enters on the night of Arafah, performs tawaf and sa‘i, then enters ihram and proceeds to Mina, there is no problem in doing so.
